question: Which hormone causes smooth muscle in the gut to relax during pregnancy?
explanation: Progesterone relaxes smooth muscle throughout the body, which slows down digestion during pregnancy. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h1)

question: How does the growing uterus affect the stomach?

options.A: It displaces the stomach upward and to the side
options.B: It flattens the stomach against the diaphragm
options.C: It compresses the liver against the abdominal wall
options.D: It pushes the stomach down into the pelvic cavity

explanation: As the uterus grows, it changes the position of nearby organs by pushing the stomach up and outward. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h1)

question: What is the medical term for heartburn during pregnancy?
explanation: Pyrosis is the clinical word for heartburn, caused by stomach acid moving back up into the food pipe. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h2)

question: A pregnant patient feels a burning sensation in her chest after eating. What causes this?

options.A: Relaxation of the lower oesophageal sphincter
options.B: Rapid emptying of food from the stomach

explanation: Progesterone relaxes the valve at the bottom of the food pipe, letting stomach acid flow upward. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h2)

question: What is the main cause of constipation in pregnant women?
explanation: High progesterone slows down bowel movements, giving the body more time to absorb water from stool. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h3)

question: Why do pregnant women often get haemorrhoids late in pregnancy?

options.A: Pressure from the large uterus on pelvic blood vessels
options.C: Fast movement of food through the gut
options.D: Extra digestive juices in the bowel

explanation: The heavy uterus puts pressure on blood vessels, and straining from constipation causes rectal veins to swell. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h3)

question: What happens to the gallbladder during a normal pregnancy?

options.A: It contracts much faster than usual
options.B: Bile flow slows down due to relaxed muscles
options.D: It gets blocked by the spleen

explanation: Progesterone makes the gallbladder less active, leading to sluggish emptying and stored bile. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h4)

question: Why are pregnant women more likely to develop gallstones?

options.A: The liver makes too much cholesterol
options.B: Stomach acid breaks down normal bile salts
options.C: Sluggish and delayed emptying concentrates the bile
options.D: The gallbladder is crushed by the liver

explanation: When bile moves too slowly, cholesterol can separate out and form stones more easily. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h4)

question: What happens to stomach emptying during active labour?

options.A: It stays the same as in early pregnancy
options.B: It speeds up to clear the gut
options.C: It slows down or stops almost completely

explanation: Labour pain, stress, and medications cause digestion and stomach emptying to pause. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h5)

question: Why is lung aspiration a major risk during emergency surgery in labour?

options.A: Food and liquid stay in the stomach because digestion has paused
options.C: Lungs fill with extra IV fluids
options.D: Bile flows backward into the lungs

explanation: Because stomach emptying stops during labour, leftover food can enter the lungs if protective reflexes drop under anaesthesia. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h5)

question: What triggers the return of normal gut function after childbirth?

options.C: A rapid drop in placental hormones
options.D: A sudden rise in body temperature

explanation: Delivering the placenta causes a quick drop in progesterone and oestrogen, removing their relaxant effects on the gut. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h6)

question: A new mother is afraid to pass stool two days after a vaginal delivery because of her episiotomy wound. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Insert a tube to clear her bowel
options.B: Tell her not to eat until she passes stool
options.C: Give her a strong enema right away
options.D: Explain that the wound is secure, and encourage fluids and stool softeners

explanation: Reassuring the patient while offering gentle stool softeners and fluids helps reduce her fear and prevents straining. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T4#GNS121_U7_T4_h6)
